source: F:\datasets voice-ai-cold-calling-skill Technique 01 (Research Survey) + Technique 02 (Customer Journey Mirror), distilled as retrieval data

handlers.title: Research survey opener
beats: Lead with a disarming survey frame, not a sales claim.
Name a small fixed question count and a two-minute cap.
Anchor locally: the survey is for businesses in their city.

handlers.title: Hesitation reassurance
beats: Narrow the topic to one concrete subject: how they handle calls.
Promise explicitly that nothing is being sold on this call.

handlers.title: Already has an answering service
beats: Ask whether it covers nights, weekends and overflows, and whether anything still lands in voicemail.
If they are happy, pivot to a referral ask instead of pushing.
If there is friction, probe the gap before saying anything about the offer.

handlers.title: Forwards everything to a cell phone
beats: Concede business-hours coverage, then ask about the other call, after hours, holidays and vacations.
They will admit some calls slip; run the pain math on those.

handlers.title: Not the owner or retired
beats: Ask who handles this and whether there is another local business worth reaching.
Take the referral path; never pitch a non-decision-maker.

handlers.title: Uncomfortable sharing numbers
beats: Accept immediately and wish them well.
Never push past discomfort; end gracefully.

handlers.title: Too small or brand new
beats: Reframe early stage as the right time to set up call handling, before missed calls pile up.
Offer to keep their details and circle back in a few months.

handlers.title: Needs a human for quotes
beats: Position the assistant as lead capture, not replacement: it gathers vehicle, service and contact details and texts them over.
The owner still handles the quote personally; they just never miss the lead.

handlers.title: Pain math
beats: Multiply missed calls per week by average ticket value out loud and ask them to confirm the figure.
Make them confront the weekly cost before any pitch.

handlers.title: Third-party soft pitch
beats: Attribute the idea to someone else and frame the call as validation, not a sale.
Cite real usage elsewhere, then the local angle.
End on the free demo offer with no commitment.

handlers.title: Demo deferral
beats: Accept the deferral without pressure.
Ask permission to text contact details so they have a local name if they change their mind.

handlers.title: Customer journey mirror close
beats: Walk them through their own buying behavior: search, first page, reviews, calling two or three businesses, picking whoever answers.
Mirror it back: their customers behave the same way.
Lock the pain: unanswered leads bounce to competitors.
Close with a question, not a pitch: ask what reason remains not to close the gap.
